newsitem.title: GERMANY: German newspaper marketing unit set to launch.
newsitem.headline: German newspaper marketing unit set to launch.

text.p: The German Association of Newspaper Publishers (BDZV) and the German Regional Press Club said on Wednesday they planned to join forces on a new organisation dedicated to newspaper marketing.

The new Frankfurt-based marketing body, to be called the Newspaper Marketing Society (ZMG), plans an aggressive campaign to recapture the edge it was in danger of losing to other media in the German advertising market, the BDZV said.

Although the newspaper industry still holds the biggest share of the German advertising market -- even topping television, BDZV Vice President Pierre Gerckens said the field was growing constantly more cut-throat.

"Our piece of the (German) advertising market pie, at the moment a third, is continually shrinking," he said. "We will soon have a situation in which a third (of the advertising market) belongs to television."

The ZMG will serve as a go-between for advertising agencies, companies which advertise and newspaper publishers to improve the accessability, coordination and performance of marketing in their field, Gerckens said.

"We will create a synergy effect with the ZMG by uniting our strengths which will maximise our impact," he added. A for-hire centre for market research and digital data transmission would also be available to clients.

The ZMG will start with a budget of seven million marks ($4 million). Participating publishers, who distribute 17 million newpapers daily, will thereafter contribute 35 pfennigs per issue or a set fee depending on their circulation.
The partners said they have not yet set a start date.

The BDZV serves as an umbrella organisation for 330 independent newspaper publishers, which it said comprised 90 percent of the nation's daily distribution of 25 million issues, among the largest of Europe's newspaper markets.
As earlier announced, the Regional Press Club will be subsumed by the BDZV and the ZMG in June.
